members.name: price_impact_reversion_v1
members.universe: NIFTY 100 constituents (focus on names ranked 51-100 for thinner liquidity)
members.thesis: Large trades (>5x median trade size) cause temporary price impact that partially reverts within 2-5 minutes. In Indian mid-cap equities where liquidity is thinner, a single large market order can push the price 10-30 bps beyond fair value. Market makers and informed traders step in to capture the re
members.exit_target: reversion to 50% of impact (e.g., if impact = -20 bps, target +10 bps)
members.exit_stop: impact extends by 50% (e.g., if impact = -20 bps, stop at -30 bps from pre-impact)
filters: India_VIX < 25; impacts in high-VIX tend to be informed (no reversion)
skip first 10 min (opening auction distorts impact measurement)
bar volume > 2x SMA(volume, 20) (confirm the large trade bar)
prefer trades against intraday trend (counter-trend reversion more reliable)
skip if bid-ask spread > 10 bps (wide spread erases reversion profit)
weaknesses: Cannot distinguish informed vs uninformed large trades with certainty. Trading against an informed institutional buyer means catching a falling knife / fighting momentum.
In NIFTY 100 stocks ranked 51-100, liquidity can dry up suddenly, making exit at target price difficult and widening actual slippage beyond the 3 bps assumption.
Result season (Jan-Feb, Apr-May, Jul-Aug, Oct-Nov) increases false signals as earnings-driven large trades are informed and don't revert.

members.name: liquidity_provision_v1
members.universe: NIFTY 50 constituents (most liquid names for tight spread capture)
members.thesis: By placing limit orders around the running VWAP, we effectively provide liquidity to participants executing VWAP algorithms. Institutional VWAP algos are the single largest source of predictable order flow in Indian equities (estimated 20-30% of institutional volume). These algos target VWAP and wil
filters: India_VIX < 18; this strategy fails in high-vol (VWAP bands widen, stops hit)
no trades in first 5 min (VWAP unstable) or last 15 min (closing pressure)
skip if volume_participation < 0.6 (abnormally low volume day)
reduce size if |VWAP_deviation_bps| > 30 (strong trend, reversion less likely)
skip if spread_ratio > 2.0 (adverse selection risk elevated)
weaknesses: Limit orders may not fill in fast-moving markets, leading to opportunity cost. In trending days, the strategy may generate zero trades.
Adverse selection: fills are more likely when informed traders push price through the limit level, meaning fills are negatively selected vs random.
Zerodha does not support placing and managing limit orders programmatically with sub-second latency; Kite API has ~200ms round-trip introducing fill risk.
members.prior_art: Avellaneda & Stoikov (2008) 'High-Frequency Trading in a Limit Order Book' — foundational market-making model. Gueant, Lehalle & Fernandez-Tapia (2012) extend to optimal inventory management. Berkowit
